cards.text: Meanwhile, out on the battlefield, there's still a war on. David stayed back in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1), but Joab, the commander of his army (2 Samuel 8:16), is fighting against Rabbah of the Ammonites.

cards.question: Joab is fighting against Rabbah of the Ammonites. What does he capture?

cards.text: Then Joab sends messengers back to David with an update from the front.

cards.question: In his message, Joab tells David he has captured the city's water supply.

cards.text: Then Joab tells David what to do next: gather the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city and capture it. And he adds a little something extra.

cards.question: Joab tells David to come and capture Rabbah. What does Joab say will happen otherwise?

answers.text: Joab will capture it and it will be named after him
The Ammonites will win back the royal fortress
The troops will give up and head back home

cards.text: WHOA, Joab! That's like a coworker texting you, "Come finish this project, or my name's going on it." So David gets moving.

cards.question: David assembles ___ of the troops and goes to Rabbah.

cards.text: David goes to Rabbah and fights against it. And he captures it!

cards.question: Rabbah has fallen. What does David take from the head of the Ammonites' king?
The king's crown weighed a talent of ___ and was set with precious stones.

cards.text: Then that crown is placed on David's head. A TALENT of gold up there, friend, and I can barely keep this chef's hat on straight!

cards.question: Besides the crown, David takes a great amount of plunder from Rabbah.

cards.text: Next, David brings out the people who were there in the city.

cards.question: David brings out the people of Rabbah. What does he do with them?

answers.text: Puts them to work with tools and at brick kilns
Sends them away to live in a far land
Makes them stand guard over the city walls

cards.question: David does this to Rabbah only and leaves the other Ammonite cities alone.
With the Ammonite cities handled, where do David and all his troops go?

findings.problem: The card is bare narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice: "Then Joab sends messengers back to David with an update from the front." It reads like a plain summary line, not Papa Dorin telling the story.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Only two cards in the whole walkthrough carry any humor: card 7, the coworker text, and card 12, the chef's hat. The other story cards read as pleasant, neutral narration, and moments like Rabbah falling in card 9 have no reaction from Papa Dorin.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says "David does this to Rabbah only". "This" points back to the forced labor from card 15, which is no longer on screen, so the question doesn't say what David did.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
